**Rosalia Vila Tobella** (born 25 September 1992), known [mononymously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mononymously "Mononymously") as **Rosalía** (Spanish:[[rosaˈli.a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"), Catalan:[[ruzəˈli.ə]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Catalan "Help:IPA/Catalan")),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-3) is a Spanish singer-songwriter and actress. She has been described as an "atypical pop star" due to her genre-bending musical style.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-4) After being enthralled by [Spanish folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_folk_music "Spanish folk music") at age 14, she studied [musicology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musicology "Musicology") at the [Catalonia College of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia_College_of_Music "Catalonia College of Music") and graduated in 2017.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-popmusic-5)

She completed her studies with [honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honors_student "Honors student") by virtue of her debut and collaborative cover album with [Raül Refree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ra%C3%BCl_Refree "Raül Refree"), _[Los Ángeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_%C3%81ngeles\_(album) "Los Ángeles (album)")_ (2017), and her [baccalaureate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baccalaureate_degree "Baccalaureate degree") second album _[El mal querer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El\_mal\_querer "El mal querer")_ (2018). Reimagining [flamenco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamenco "Flamenco") by mixing it with [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") and [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop") music, it spawned the singles "[Malamente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malamente "Malamente")" and "[Pienso en tu mirá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pienso_en_tu_mir%C3%A1 "Pienso en tu mirá")", which caught the attention of the Spanish public, and were released to critical acclaim.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-petridis-6) A recipient of the [Latin Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award "Latin Grammy Award") for [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Latin Grammy Award for Album of the Year") and listed in [_Rolling Stone_'s 500 Greatest Albums of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_500_Greatest_Albums_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time"), _El mal querer_ started the ascent of Rosalía into the international music scene.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-500mejores-8) Rosalía explored [urbano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbano_music "Urbano music") music with her 2019 releases "[Con altura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Con_altura "Con altura")" and "[Yo x ti, tú x mí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yo_x_ti,_t%C3%BA_x_m%C3%AD "Yo x ti, tú x mí")", achieving global success.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-10) She gave [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") an [experimental twist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_reggaeton "Alternative reggaeton") on her third studio album _[Motomami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motomami "Motomami")_ (2022), departing from the [new flamenco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_flamenco "New flamenco") sound of its predecessor. The album caught international attention with its singles "[La Fama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Fama_(song) "La Fama (song)")", "[Saoko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saoko "Saoko")", and "[Despechá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despech%C3%A1 "Despechá")", to become the best reviewed album of the year on [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-pitchfork-12) Her fourth album _[Lux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lux\_(Rosal%C3%ADa\_album) "Lux (Rosalía album)")_ (2025) broke several all-time records by a Spanish-speaking female artist and was widely acclaimed by critics for its fusion of [art pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_pop "Art pop") and [classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_music "Classical music") elements.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-auto-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-auto1-16)

In the course of her career, Rosalía has accumulated [thirteen number-ones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_artists_who_reached_number_one_on_the_Spanish_Singles_Chart "List of artists who reached number one on the Spanish Singles Chart") in her home country, the most for a local female artist. She [has also won](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Rosal%C3%ADa "List of awards and nominations received by Rosalía") two [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards"), eleven [Latin Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Awards "Latin Grammy Awards") (including two [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Latin Grammy Award for Album of the Year") wins), a [BRIT Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Awards "Brit Awards"), four [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Awards "MTV Video Music Awards"), two [MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "MTV Europe Music Awards"), three [UK Music Video Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Music_Video_Awards "UK Music Video Awards"), an [Ivor Novello Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards "Ivor Novello Awards") and two [Premio Ruido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Ruido "Premio Ruido") awards, among others. In 2019, _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_ gave her the [Rising Star Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Women_in_Music "Billboard Women in Music") for "changing the sound of today's mainstream music with her fresh flamenco-influenced pop",[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-:2-17) and became the first Spanish-singing act in history to be nominated for [Best New Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist") at the Grammys.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-spanishlatimes-18) She is widely considered one of the most successful and influential Spanish singers of all time.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-20)

## Life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rosal%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")]

### 1992–2016: Early life and career beginnings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rosal%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1992–2016: Early life and career beginnings")]

Rosalía Vila Tobella was born in 1992 at a hospital in [Sant Cugat del Vallès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sant_Cugat_del_Vall%C3%A8s "Sant Cugat del Vallès"), Catalonia, although she was raised in [Sant Esteve Sesrovires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sant_Esteve_Sesrovires "Sant Esteve Sesrovires"), [Baix Llobregat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baix_Llobregat "Baix Llobregat").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-21) Born to a family with no musical background, she was named after her maternal grandmother Rosalía Aguilera Torres, who was born in [Òdena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%92dena "Òdena").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-22) She is the youngest daughter of María Pilar Tobella Aguilera, who runs Suprametal, SA, a family company specialising in metalworks for windows. Her father, José Manuel Vila, was born in [Cudillero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cudillero "Cudillero"), [Asturias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asturias "Asturias"), to a [Galician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galician_people "Galician people") father from [Vigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vigo "Vigo") and a mother from [Ávila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81vila "Ávila"), with one of his grandfathers being born in [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-emr-23) Her parents [separated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_separation "Legal separation") in 2019.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-24) Rosalía has an older sister, Pilar "Pili" Vila (born 1989), who works with her as her stylist and creative director.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-25)

Rosalía expressed interest in the performing arts at an early age, especially after discovering the discography of [Camarón de la Isla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camar%C3%B3n_de_la_Isla "Camarón de la Isla"). She began her musical education at the Taller de Músics.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-26), where she completed a six-year course. She then began attending class at the [Raval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Raval "El Raval") school, later transferring to the [Superior School of Music of Catalonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia_College_of_Music "Catalonia College of Music").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-27) She graduated in 2017.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-popmusic-5) During this time, she also worked as an independent singer at weddings and musical bars, for which she was paid "a little over 80 [euros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro "Euro") or in exchange for [dinner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinner "Dinner")".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-popmusic-5) During that time, Rosalía met many [underground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underground_music "Underground music") Spanish artists who would later become successful, such as [La Zowi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Zowi "La Zowi"), [Yung Beef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yung_Beef "Yung Beef"), [Kaydy Cain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaydy_Cain "Kaydy Cain"), [Hinds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinds_(band) "Hinds (band)") and María Escarmiento.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-28)

At 15, she competed on the television show _Tú Sí Que Vales_, although she was not selected. At 17, she had to undergo vocal cord surgery after tearing one of her vocal cords due to "intense singing practices" and was unable to sing for a year.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-29) In 2012, she became the vocalist of Kejaleo, a flamenco music group featuring Jordi Franco, Roger Blavia, Cristo Fontecilla, Diego Cortés and Xavi Turull.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-30) They released an album, _Alaire_, in 2013. That same year, Rosalía professionally worked as a duo with [Juan "Chicuelo" Gómez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicuelo_(guitarist) "Chicuelo (guitarist)") to promote the _[Blancanieves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blancanieves "Blancanieves")_ soundtrack at the 2013 Panama International Film Festival in substitution of [Sílvia Pérez Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%ADlvia_P%C3%A9rez_Cruz "Sílvia Pérez Cruz") and at the [Festival Grec de Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival_Grec_de_Barcelona "Festival Grec de Barcelona") for the contemporary dance work _De Carmen_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-31) In 2013, she participated in the [Association of Performing Arts Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Performing_Arts_Professionals "Association of Performing Arts Professionals") (APAP) Conference in New York, and was the lead voice in the culmination of the Any Espriu 2014. In 2015, she collaborated with [La Fura dels Baus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Fura_dels_Baus "La Fura dels Baus") on a show that premiered in [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-32) She was the opening act for flamenco artist [Miguel Poveda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Poveda "Miguel Poveda"), accompanied by Alfredo Lagos, at the International Music Festival of Cadaqués, and also at the 2016 Jerez Jazz Festival. She worked with [Rocío Márquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roc%C3%ADo_M%C3%A1rquez "Rocío Márquez") on the presentation of her album _El Niño_, produced by [Raül Refree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ra%C3%BCl_Refree "Raül Refree"), at [Primavera Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primavera_Sound "Primavera Sound"). In 2015, she also worked with clothing brand [Desigual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desigual "Desigual") and sang the single for their campaign jingle "Last Night Was Eternal". and self-released "Un Millón de Veces" included in the benefit album _Tres Guitarras Para el Autismo_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-33) At 20, she worked as a flamenco teacher and vocal coach.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-34) In 2016, Rosalía collaborated with Spanish rapper and former boyfriend [C. Tangana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._Tangana "C. Tangana") on "[Antes de morirme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antes_de_morirme "Antes de morirme")".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-35) The song was a [sleeper hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper_hit "Sleeper hit") and entered the [Spanish Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Productores_de_M%C3%BAsica_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Productores de Música de España") in 2018, after the success of Rosalía's newer material. The collaboration received international attention when it was featured on the soundtrack of the first season of the Spanish [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") show _[Élite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elite\_(TV\_series) "Elite (TV series)")_.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-36)

### 2016–2017: _Los Ángeles_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rosal%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2016–2017: Los Ángeles")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/El_flamenco_de_Rosal%C3%ADa_y_Ra%C3%BAl_Refree_llena_el_Parque_de_la_Cu%C3%B1a_Verde_%2803%29.jpg/330px-El_flamenco_de_Rosal%C3%ADa_y_Ra%C3%BAl_Refree_llena_el_Parque_de_la_Cu%C3%B1a_Verde_%2803%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:El_flamenco_de_Rosal%C3%ADa_y_Ra%C3%BAl_Refree_llena_el_Parque_de_la_Cu%C3%B1a_Verde_(03).jpg)

Rosalía and Raül Refree during Los Ángeles Tour in July 2017

In 2016, Rosalía performed to a crowd of a hundred people at the Tablao del Carmen, a flamenco specialised venue at the [Pueblo Español](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poble_Espanyol "Poble Espanyol"), in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"). In the audience was [Raül Refree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ra%C3%BCl_Refree "Raül Refree"), whom she invited to the show.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-37) They began working on two albums together.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-38) Rosalía signed with [Universal Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") later in 2016, and she relocated to [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-allmusicbio2-39) She went on to only release _[Los Ángeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_%C3%A1ngeles\_(album) "Los ángeles (album)")_.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-40) The album talks about death in a dark way with aggressive guitar chords by Refree.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-41) It presents reworks of flamenco classics receiving several accolades.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-mejoresABC-42) She was nominated for [Best New Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Latin Grammy Award for Best New Artist") at the [18th Latin Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/18th_Annual_Latin_Grammy_Awards "18th Annual Latin Grammy Awards"). The album was released on 10 February 2017 through Universal Music and spawned two singles, "Catalina", released in October 2016, and "[De Plata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Plata "De Plata")", released in May 2017. The album was very well received by critics. Jordi Bardají wrote in 2018 that the record was "one of the greatest '[sleepers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper_hit "Sleeper hit")' that Spanish sales lists have known in recent times." _Los Ángeles_ reached its peak position of number nine on 11 November 2018 and has remained in the albums chart since its entry, having accumulated a total of 89 weeks. _Los Ángeles_ won the "Album of the Year" award at the [Time Out Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Out_(magazine) "Time Out (magazine)") and the [Premio Ruido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Ruido "Premio Ruido"), among others.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-43) In 2017, [RTVE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RTVE "RTVE") contacted Rosalía to participate in the pre-selection to [represent Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest_2017 "Spain in the Eurovision Song Contest 2017") in the [Eurovision Song Contest 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2017 "Eurovision Song Contest 2017"), which she declined because of scheduling conflicts with the promotion of her debut record.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-45)

Rosalía and Raül Refree embarked on a concert tour, Los Ángeles Tour, supporting their first studio album together. The tour began on 11 February 2017 in [Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granada "Granada") and ended on 1 March 2018 at the [Palau de la Música](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palau_de_la_M%C3%BAsica_Catalana "Palau de la Música Catalana") in Barcelona.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-46) Spanish singer [Bebe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bebe_(singer) "Bebe (singer)") attended one of their concerts in Madrid alongside [Juanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juanes "Juanes"), who became "immediately obsessed with Rosalía" and asked his manager Rebeca León to work with her.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-47) She agreed to manage her as she felt like she was a "once in fifty years kind of artist".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-48)

### 2018–2020: _El mal querer_ and international recognition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rosal%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2018–2020: El mal querer and international recognition")]

The recording cycle for Rosalía's second studio album, _[El mal querer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El\_mal\_querer "El mal querer")_, began in early 2017 as her [baccalaureate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baccalaureate_degree "Baccalaureate degree") project, graduating from the [Catalonia College of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalonia_College_of_Music "Catalonia College of Music").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-49) She personally chose to work alongside Spanish musician [el Guincho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Guincho "El Guincho") and spawned its concept alongside friend Ferran Echegaray, who bet on the _[Romance of Flamenca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance\_of\_Flamenca "Romance of Flamenca")_ to follow the album's storyline. Despite having no [budget](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budget "Budget") to produce the record as she was an [independent artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_music "Independent music") working on a university project, Rosalía invested a lot of her own money, to the point of "almost going [bankrupt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bankruptcy "Bankruptcy")". The album was almost completely recorded at el Guincho's apartment in Barcelona with a computer, a microphone and a [sound card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_interface "Audio interface"). It would mix traditional [flamenco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamenco_music "Flamenco music") with today's [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") and [urban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_music "Urban music") music.

In May 2018, the singer announced the title of her upcoming album in a little homemade [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") series.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-50)[J Balvin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J_Balvin "J Balvin") parallelly released his fifth studio album, _[Vibras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibras\_(album) "Vibras (album)")_, which featured Rosalía on the track "[Brillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brillo_(song) "Brillo (song)")". Later that month, Rosalía released the album's lead single "[Malamente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malamente "Malamente")". The single caught the attention of international personalities such as [Kourtney Kardashian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kourtney_Kardashian "Kourtney Kardashian") and [Dua Lipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dua_Lipa "Dua Lipa"), alongside numerous music critics, while its [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_(company) "Canada (company)")-directed music video reached social media virality.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-52) The song was nominated for five [Latin Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Awards "Latin Grammy Awards"), out of it won two, for [Best Alternative Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Best_Alternative_Song "Latin Grammy Award for Best Alternative Song") and for [Best Urban Fusion/Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Best_Urban_Fusion/Performance "Latin Grammy Award for Best Urban Fusion/Performance"). The follow-up single, "[Pienso en tu mirá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pienso_en_tu_mir%C3%A1 "Pienso en tu mirá")", was released in July. Its music video received critical acclaim for its aesthetics and poetic symbolism.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-54) The song was nominated for Best Pop Song at the [2019 Latin Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Annual_Latin_Grammy_Awards "20th Annual Latin Grammy Awards"). The third single, "[Di mi nombre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Di_mi_nombre "Di mi nombre")", released three days prior to the album, earned Rosalía her first number-one single in Spain.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-55)

_El mal querer_ was released on 2 November 2018 and debuted at number two on the [PROMUSICAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Productores_de_M%C3%BAsica_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Productores de Música de España") chart. Presented as experimental and conceptual, it revolves around a toxic relationship described in the anonymous 13th-century [Occitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occitan_language "Occitan language") novel _[Flamenca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance\_of\_Flamenca "Romance of Flamenca")_.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-56) The album was met with universal acclaim by [music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_journalism "Music journalism"). Writing for _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_, head critic [Alexis Petridis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Petridis "Alexis Petridis") highly commended the album, giving it the highest rating and describing it as "the calling card of a unique new talent".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-petridis-6)_El mal querer_ was listed in over twenty album year-end and decade-end lists by publications such as _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork\_(website) "Pitchfork (website)")_, _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_ and _The Guardian_.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-58)_[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ listed it 315th on their [500 Greatest Albums of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_500_Greatest_Albums_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time") list, making it the highest Spanish-language album in the list.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-59)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-500mejores-8)_El mal querer_ was later nominated for several awards including four [Latin Grammys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award "Latin Grammy Award"), a [Latin _Billboard_ Music award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Billboard_Music_Awards "Latin Billboard Music Awards"), a [Latin American Music award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_American_Music_Awards "Latin American Music Awards") and a [LOS40 Music award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LOS40_Music_Awards "LOS40 Music Awards"). It also won the [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") for [Best Latin Rock, Urban or Alternative Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Latin_Rock,_Urban_or_Alternative_Album "Grammy Award for Best Latin Rock, Urban or Alternative Album").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-60)

In 2019 Rosalía took part in the [Pedro Almodóvar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Almod%C3%B3var "Pedro Almodóvar") film _[Pain and Glory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pain\_and\_Glory "Pain and Glory")_.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-62) She had previously contributed vocals to the soundtracks of _[Arde Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arde\_Madrid "Arde Madrid")_ and _[Paquita Salas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paquita\_Salas "Paquita Salas")_.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-64) In March 2019, Rosalía embarked on her first global concert tour, [El Mal Querer Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal_Querer_Tour "El Mal Querer Tour"), to further promote _El Mal Querer_, with shows in South America, North America, Europe and Africa.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-67)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Rosalia%2C_Pull%26Bear_stage_2.jpg/330px-Rosalia%2C_Pull%26Bear_stage_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rosalia,_Pull&Bear_stage_2.jpg)

Rosalía performing at [Primavera Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primavera_Sound "Primavera Sound") in 2019 during El Mal Querer Tour

While on tour, Rosalía issued several songs. On 28 March 2019, she released a second collaboration with Balvin, "[Con altura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Con_altura "Con altura")". Despite initially receiving mixed reviews from critics, "Con altura" topped the charts in Argentina, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, Venezuela and Spain. Its music video, directed by [Director X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_X "Director X"), became the most-watched music video by a female artist of 2019.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-69) It also spawned her nickname "La Rosalía" and its choreography eventually became viral and a moment in [Latin pop culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_culture "Popular culture").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-70) "Con altura" won two [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award "MTV Video Music Award") for [Best Latin Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Latino_Artist "MTV Video Music Award for Best Latino Artist") and [Best Choreography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Choreography "MTV Video Music Award for Best Choreography"), making her the first Spanish act to win one.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-71) It also won [Best Collaboration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Collaboration "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Collaboration") at the 2019 [MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award "MTV Europe Music Award") and [Best Urban Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Best_Urban_Song "Latin Grammy Award for Best Urban Song") at the [2019 Latin Grammys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Annual_Latin_Grammy_Awards "20th Annual Latin Grammy Awards").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-72) The song has sold over seven million copies worldwide so far.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-73)

In May, Rosalía released the song "[Aute Cuture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aute_Cuture "Aute Cuture")".[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-74) It became her third number-one in Spain and earned a Latin Grammy nomination for [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Latin Grammy Award for Record of the Year").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-75) In July, she released the single _[Fucking Money Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fucking\_Money\_Man "Fucking Money Man")_, which includes two tracks: "[Milionària](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milion%C3%A0ria "Milionària")" (which she sang in [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_language "Catalan language")) and "[Dios nos libre del dinero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dios_nos_libre_del_dinero "Dios nos libre del dinero")".[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-76) On 15 August, she released her collaboration with [Ozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozuna_(singer) "Ozuna (singer)") "[Yo x ti, tú x mí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yo_x_ti,_t%C3%BA_x_m%C3%AD "Yo x ti, tú x had worked earlier with on "[Barefoot in the Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barefoot_in_the_Park_(song) "Barefoot in the Park (song)")".[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-79) In December, Rosalía was featured alongside [Lil ### 2020–2023: Collaborations and _Motomami_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rosal%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2020–2023: Collaborations and Motomami")]

Recording sessions for Rosalía's third studio album started as early as 2019. Due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Rosalía relocated to [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami") where she continued to work on the album while also providing vocals to multiple songs.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-90) On 4 September 2020, a remix of [Sech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sech_(singer) "Sech (singer)")'s "[Relación](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relaci%C3%B3n_(song) "Relación (song)")", which also features [Daddy Yankee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daddy_Yankee "Daddy Yankee"), [Farruko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farruko "Farruko") and [J Balvin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J_Balvin "J Balvin"), was released, earning Rosalía her second entry on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), peaking at 64.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-91) She also took part in [Bad Bunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Bunny "Bad Bunny")'s third solo studio album, _[El Último Tour del Mundo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El\_%C3%9Altimo\_Tour\_Del\_Mundo "El Último Tour Del Mundo")_, on the track "[La Noche de Anoche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Noche_de_Anoche "La Noche de Anoche")", which was later released as a single on [Valentine's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentine's_Day "Valentine's Day").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-:1-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-93) The collaboration, performed on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday\_Night\_Live\_(season\_46) "Saturday Night Live (season 46)")_, became a huge commercial success, debuting at number two on the Spotify global chart with 6.63 million streams in a single day, marking the biggest debut for a song fully sung in Spanish in history.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-94) A week later, she collaborated alongside [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") on the remix of "[Blinding Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blinding_Lights "Blinding Lights")" and, in January, with [Billie Eilish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Eilish "Billie Eilish") on "[Lo Vas a Olvidar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo_Vas_a_Olvidar "Lo Vas a Olvidar")", which was featured in the _[Euphoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphoria\_(American\_TV\_series) "Euphoria (American TV series)")_ special episode "[Fuck Anyone Who's Not a Sea Blob](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuck_Anyone_Who's_Not_a_Sea_Blob "Fuck Anyone Who's Not a Sea Blob")".[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-96) Rosalía later collaborated with [Oneohtrix Point Never](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oneohtrix_Point_Never "Oneohtrix Point Never") and [Tokischa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokischa "Tokischa") on "Nothing's Special" and "[Linda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_(Tokischa_and_Rosal%C3%ADa_song) "Linda (Tokischa and Rosalía song)")" respectively.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-98)

On 2 November 2021, Rosalía announced the title of her new album _[Motomami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motomami "Motomami")_.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-99) It was released on 18 March 2022 through [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records"). Promotion prior to the album release encompassed the release of three singles and the promotional singles "[Hentai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hentai_(song) "Hentai (song)")" and "[Candy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candy_(Rosal%C3%ADa_song) "Candy (Rosalía song)")". The lead single "[La Fama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Fama_(song) "La Fama (song)")", featuring [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd"), is an [experimental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_music "Experimental music")[bachata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachata_(music) "Bachata (music)") that saw great commercial success. It became Rosalía's [seventh number one single in Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_artists_who_reached_number_one_on_the_Spanish_Singles_Chart "List of artists who reached number one on the Spanish Singles Chart") while also peaking at five in France and reaching the top ten spot in eight other countries. In December 2021, [Rockstar Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockstar_Games "Rockstar Games") launched a new _[Grand Theft Auto Online](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand\_Theft\_Auto\_Online "Grand Theft Auto Online")_ radio station, Motomami Los Santos, curated by Rosalía and [Arca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arca_(musician) "Arca (musician)").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-100) In February 2022, Rosalía revealed the album artwork for _Motomami_ and released "[Saoko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saoko "Saoko")" as the album's second single to wide critical acclaim.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-101) The song's accompanying music video, directed by Valentin Petit, was shot in [Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv "Kyiv"), mainly at [Podilskyi Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Podilskyi_Bridge "Podilskyi Bridge").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-Rolling_Stone-102) For its editing done by Petit and Jon Echeveste, the video would go on to win the [MTV Video Music Award for Best Editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Editing "MTV Video Music Award for Best Editing"). On 24 February, Rosalía released "[Chicken Teriyaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken_Teriyaki_(song) "Chicken Teriyaki (song)")" as the album's third single.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-103)

Rosalía performing on her [Motomami World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motomami_World_Tour "Motomami World Tour")

Upon release, _Motomami_ received universal acclaim from [music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_journalism "Music journalism"), many of whom praised the experimentation and genre-bending sounds. _Motomami_ received a perfect score from various publications, including _[The Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Telegraph\_(London) "The Telegraph (London)")_, _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Independent "The Independent")_ and _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ and was given four stars or more by _[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash\_(magazine) "Clash (magazine)")_, _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_, _[Rockdelux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockdelux "Rockdelux")_, _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ etc. _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork\_(website) "Pitchfork (website)")_ crowned _Motomami_ with its "Best New Music" honour writing, "It feels rare to hear an album that's so experimental, that aspires to stretch itself out across genres and play with form, and that attains exactly what it sets out to achieve. Rosalía was already a formidable singer, but here she also sounds like she learned that with global superstardom comes the freedom to set her own agenda".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-pitchfork-12) The album has become the best reviewed and most discussed album of 2022 on [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic").[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-104) Commercially, _Motomami_ entered twenty-two charts in nineteen countries and reached the top ten in seven countries, two of them number-ones. The album entered major market charts, reaching the top forty in both on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") and the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"). On [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), it achieved the biggest debut for a Spanish-language album by a female artist on the platform's history, with 16.3 million streams in the first day.

In July 2022, Rosalía embarked on her second worldwide concert tour, [Motomami World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motomami_World_Tour "Motomami World Tour"), to further promote _Motomami_, with shows in Europe, South America and North America. The setlist featured four unreleased tracks including "[Despechá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despech%C3%A1 "Despechá")", which was later released on 28 July to global success.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-105) Rosalía later took part in the forthcoming projects by [Romeo Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romeo_Santos "Romeo Santos"), Niño de Elche, and [Wisin & Yandel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisin_&_Yandel "Wisin & Yandel").[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-108)

At the [23rd Annual Latin Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/23rd_Annual_Latin_Grammy_Awards "23rd Annual Latin Grammy Awards"), _Motomami_ won the four categories in which it was nominated in, which were [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Latin Grammy Award for Album of the Year"), [Best Alternative Music Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Best_Alternative_Music_Album "Latin Grammy Award for Best Alternative Music Album"), [Best Engineered Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Best_Engineered_Album "Latin Grammy Award for Best Engineered Album") and [Best Recording Package](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Grammy_Award_for_Best_Recording_Package "Latin Grammy Award for Best Recording Package"). Rosalía was the first woman and sixth act overall to win Album of the Year twice as a lead artist.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-109) She also received two nominations at the [65th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "65th Annual Grammy Awards") for [Best Latin Rock or Alternative Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Latin_Rock_or_Alternative_Album "Grammy Award for Best Latin Rock or Alternative Album") and [Best Music Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Music_Film "Grammy Award for Best Music Film") for Motomami TikTok Live, winning for the former category. However, media such as _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_, [_Pitchfork_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_(website) "Pitchfork (website)"), the [_New York Times_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times") and [_W_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W_(magazine) "W (magazine)") believed that the Recording Academy and the Grammys had snubbed _Motomami_ for the [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") category.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-110)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-113)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rosal%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Artistry")]

### Musical style and genres

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rosal%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Musical style and genres")]

Noted for the conceptuality and constant genre transformation of her albums and singles, Rosalía's music has evolved from [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") to the mainstream and [avant-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avant-pop "Avant-pop"). As Rosalía has a [master's degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master's_degree "Master's degree") in [flamenco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamenco "Flamenco") interpretation, she started her professional career as a full flamenco singer. 2017 saw the release of her debut album _[Los Ángeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_%C3%81ngeles\_(album) "Los Ángeles (album)")_, a folk record in which Rosalía "is posited as the contemporary _[cantaora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantaor "Cantaor")_ who has better understood the current times".[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-145) The singer has, ever since, been described as "an old soul trapped in a young body" due to the maturity of the genre.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-146) After the release of "[Malamente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malamente "Malamente")" in May 2018, which rose the singer's popularity to a national level, her music was described as a "heavily exciting [fusion of flamenco and modern arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_flamenco "New flamenco")". American magazine [_Pitchfork_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_Media "Pitchfork Media") called the singer's voice "a soft liquid velvet" and wrote that "Malamente consumes the listener with drums and soft synthesizers that drag you to their world completely". After releasing _El mal querer_ later that year, _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ gave it a perfect score and stated: "the Catalan singer's potent, smart second album is more complex than any Latin pop currently in the charts".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-petridis-6) During the three-year droplet era that started with the 2019 release "[Con altura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Con_altura "Con altura")", Rosalía's music evolved to a more mainstream urbano field without leaving the flamenco essence that characterises her artistry.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-147) Described by _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ as "one of the most daring and reckless productions of recent years", Rosalía's 2022 studio album _[Motomami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motomami "Motomami")_ "redefined mainstream" by taking [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") as its main influence and blending it with [traditional music of Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Latin_America "Music of Latin America") as well as with other genres such as [industrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_music "Industrial music") or [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz").[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-148) The singer has stated that she listens to a vast catalogue of music specially when she is making a record in the urge to learn about them. Rosalía has cited the [2011 eponymous album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Blake_(album) "James Blake (album)") by [James Blake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Blake_(musician) "James Blake (musician)") as one of the most impactful records of her life.

In his _El mal querer_ review, _The Guardian_'s [Alexis Petridis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Petridis "Alexis Petridis") wrote: "She can really sing [...] but her voice is audibly rooted in a different musical tradition to the usual styles in which pop vocalists perform. The standard set of tricks (post-[Whitney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitney_Houston "Whitney Houston")[extemporisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extemporisation "Extemporisation") overload, sub-[Winehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Winehouse "Amy Winehouse") aged [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music"), please-compare-me-to-[Kate-Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Bush "Kate Bush") kooky swooping, etc) are all noticeable by their absence. Instead, her voice is powerful and gutsily emotive: her [melismas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melismas "Melismas") sound more [Middle Eastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Eastern_music "Middle Eastern music") than [Mariah Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey")."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-petridis-6) With a naturally wide vocal range and accuracy, Rosalía also tends to use [Auto-Tune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auto-Tune "Auto-Tune") for aesthetic effects in songs and live performances.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-149)

Rosalía has been accused of cultural appropriation by some [Romani people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gitanos "Gitanos") because she adapts [Romani customs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_culture "Romani culture") into her style and draws from the flamenco music tradition, which is often thought to be from Romani people in [Andalusia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andalusia "Andalusia"). However, the origin of flamenco music is not known precisely, and it probably fused musical practices from three sources: [Moorish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moors "Moors"), [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Spain "History of the Jews in Spain") and Romani cultures. Responding to this criticism, Rosalía said, "music is universal."[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-150)

Rosalía has cited [Camarón de la Isla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camar%C3%B3n_de_la_Isla "Camarón de la Isla"), [James Blake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Blake_(musician) "James Blake (musician)") and [Björk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bj%C3%B6rk "Björk") as her major musical influences. In 2019 she told [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") "when I was 13 years old I started listening to him [Camarón de la Isla] by chance. This genre, flamenco, was what my high-school friends listened to and so did I. When I discovered him I was like 'oh my God!' I didn't think anyone was capable to sing with such a voice; it would go right through me so heartily. He was my introduction to flamenco. Thanks to him I discovered this vast universe within this music style which is almost endless and very exciting." Another flamenco influence of Rosalía is [La Niña de los Peines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Ni%C3%B1a_de_los_Peines "La Niña de los Peines"). She states that despite not enjoying her recordings at first, she ended up appreciating her melodies and realised that she was a true pioneer since most flamenco singers were men at the time she became popular. She said: "flamenco is a masculine art form by tradition and there she was, with all her creativity as a woman. She became a professional at the time when it was very unusual".[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-151)

About [Björk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bj%C3%B6rk "Björk"), Rosalía told _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork\_(website) "Pitchfork (website)")_ that she "thanks God for Björk's existence" and for "paving the way for female producers".[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-152)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosal%C3%ADa#cite_note-153) When asked about James Blake's impact on her, she said: "I started listening to him when I was at university. His music has left a mark on me; not only the bold character of his production but also its minimalism and free structures. When I listen to him, I can feel that he allows himself a lot of freedom. I personally think that he doesn't do music to please nobody but only for himself." Rosalía collaborated with Blake on his song "[Barefoot in the Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barefoot_in_the_Park_(song) "Barefoot in the Park (song)")", which was released as the fourth single of his 2019 album _[Assume Form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assume\_Form "Assume Form")_.  #### [3. Logan Lerman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0503567/?ref_=ls_t_3)

[The Perks of Being a Wallflower (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1659337/?ref_=ls_knf_3)

One of today's leading talents across both independent and mainstream film, Logan Lerman is an immensely talented actor who takes on challenging roles and brings dynamic characters to life on screen.  
  
Logan was born in Beverly Hills, to a Jewish family. His parents are Lisa (Goldman), who worked as his manager, and Larry Lerman, an orthotist and businessman. He has two siblings, Lindsey and Lucas, both older. His family operates the orthotics and prosthetics company Lerman & Son, which was founded by his great-grandfather, Jacob Lerman.  
  
When he was two and a half years old, Logan told his mother that he wanted to be an actor. At the age of four, Logan had an agent and was booked for two commercials. He made his big screen debut as William, the youngest son of [Mel Gibson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000154/?ls)'s character, in [Roland Emmerich](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000386/?ls)'s war drama [The Patriot (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0187393/?ls), and then appeared as the younger version of Gibson's character Nick Marshall in [Nancy Meyers](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0583600/?ls)'s romantic comedy [What Women Want (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0207201/?ls). After a small role in 2001's [Riding in Cars with Boys (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0200027/?ls) by [Penny Marshall](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001508/?ls), he starred in the [John Grisham](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001300/?ls) adaptation [A Painted House (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0362001/?ls), a made-for-television film that won him the first of his three Young Artist Awards.  
  
Logan played the younger version of [Ashton Kutcher](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005110/?ls)'s character, Evan, in [The Butterfly Effect (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0289879/?ls). After a guest-starring role in [10-8: Officers on Duty (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0365969/?ls), he starred in the WB Network's series [Jack & Bobby (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0410997/?ls), where he portrays Bobby (Robert) McCallister, a teenager who will grow up to be President of the United States. After the show's cancellation in 2005, Logan returned to film, starring in the family adventure [Hoot (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0453494/?ls). The next year, he played the son of Walter Sparrow ([Jim Carrey](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000120/?ls)) in the dark thriller [The Number 23 (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0481369/?ls), and co-starred with [Russell Crowe](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000128/?ls) and [Christian Bale](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000288/?ls) in [James Mangold](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0003506/?ls)'s critically-acclaimed Western remake [3:10 to Yuma (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0381849/?ls). His next two roles were a foul-mouthed private school student in the comedy [Meet Bill (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0790623/?ls) and actor [George Hamilton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001313/?ls) in the period drama [My One and Only (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1185431/?ls). Both were independent films that received limited releases. Also in 2009, Logan appeared with [Gerard Butler](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0124930/?ls) in the R-rated action thriller [Gamer (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1034032/?ls), as a foul-mouthed teenager who controls Butler's character in a real-life video game.  
  
In 2010, Logan starred as Percy in the fantasy adventure [Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0814255/?ls), based on the best-selling young adult book series of the same title. The film gave him notice among a wider audience. Subsequently, he starred as D'Artagnan in a remake of [The Three Musketeers (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1509767/?ls), which was Logan's grandfather's favorite childhood book. Lerman then headlined the coming-of-age indie drama [The Perks of Being a Wallflower (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1659337/?ls), alongside [Emma Watson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0914612/?ls), [Paul Rudd](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0748620/?ls) and [Ezra Miller](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3009232/?ls), based on the 1999 novel of the same name. Perks garnered numerous nominations and wins at the People's Choice Awards, The Independent Spirit Awards and the Teen Choice Awards, and Logan received a 2013 Teen Choice Award for Choice Movie Actor in a Drama. Around this time, he had a supporting role in the independent film [Stuck in Love. (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2205697/?ls), and returned to star in [Percy Jackson: Sea of Monsters (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1854564/?ls).  
  
His first 2014 role was in [Darren Aronofsky](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004716/?ls)'s acclaimed Biblical epic film [Noah (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1959490/?ls), playing one of the title character's sons, Ham. The film, also starring [Russell Crowe](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000128/?ls), [Jennifer Connelly](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000124/?ls), [Anthony Hopkins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000164/?ls), [Douglas Booth](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3150488/?ls), and [Emma Watson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0914612/?ls), grossed over $100 million at the North American box office. Logan next starred with [Brad Pitt](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000093/?ls), [Shia LaBeouf](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0479471/?ls), [Jon Bernthal](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1256532/?ls), and [Michael Peña](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0671567/?ls) in the World War II-set action drama [Fury (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2713180/?ls); in the film, he played one of several American soldiers engaged in tank combat against the German forces during the last weeks of the Nazi regime.  
  
Lerman next played the lead in writer-director [James Schamus](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0770005/?ls)'s 1950s-set drama [Indignation (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt4193394/?ls). Logan received rave reviews for his performance as Marcus Messner, an idealistic Jewish atheist from Newark who travels to Ohio to study at a conservative Midwestern Lutheran college. The film is based on [Philip Roth](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0744980/?ls)'s bestselling novel of the same name, and premiered at 2016's Sundance Film Festival.  
  
In 2018, Logan voiced real-life soldier Robert Conroy in [Sgt. Stubby: An American Hero (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt5314190/?ls), about the famous World War I war dog. He began the 2020s starring with Al Pacino and Josh Radnor in the stylish television drama [Hunters (2020)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt7456722/?ls), playing Jonah Heidelbaum, a Brooklyn teenager who joins a group hunting down escaped Nazis. His upcoming roles include Sean Fogle in the Irish-set drama [End of Sentence (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6910006/?ls), with [John Hawkes](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0370035/?ls) as his character's father, and Fred Nemser in the thriller [Shirley (2020)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8430598/?ls).  
  
When Logan is not working, he likes to play soccer and baseball. He is an LA Lakers fan.

[Twilight (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1099212/?ref_=ls_knf_10)

Taylor Daniel Lautner was born in Grand Rapids, Michigan, to Deborah, a software company worker, and Daniel Lautner, a pilot for Midwest Airlines. He and his younger sister Makena were raised in a well-mannered, Roman Catholic household in Hudsonville, Michigan. He is of English, German, Dutch, and Scottish descent. At the age of six, Taylor began studying martial arts at Fabiano's Karate School and he, along with his family, quickly noticed his unique and natural talent for the sport. He was soon invited to train with seven-time world karate champion Michael Chaturantabut (aka Mike Chat) and, at the age of eight, he was asked to represent his country in the 12-years-and-under division in the World Karate Association, where he became the Junior World Forms and Weapons champion, winning three gold medals. In 2003, Taylor continued to flourish in the martial arts circuit where he ranked number one in the world for NASKA's Black Belt Open Forms, Musical Weapons, Traditional Weapons, and Traditional Forms and, at the age of 12, he became the three-time Junior World Champion.  
  
However, in addition to his love for martial arts, Taylor quickly developed a love for acting at the age of seven years old when his martial arts instructor, who was involved in show business, encouraged him to audition for a small appearance in a Burger King commercial. Although he was unsuccessful, he enjoyed the experience so much that he told his parents that he wanted to pursue a career in acting. Soon, he and his family were traveling back and forth from their home in Michigan to California so Taylor could regularly audition for acting roles. When Taylor was 10, with the frequent traveling and air fares starting to become overwhelming, his family made the crucial decision to relocate to Los Angeles, where Taylor would have the advantage of being able to audition for films, television, and commercials full-time.  
  
Once Taylor moved with his family to Los Angeles, he found himself landing more and more small acting roles. He booked many occurring roles on various television shows such as [My Wife and Kids (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0273855/?ls), [Summerland (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0400037/?ls), and [The Bernie Mac Show (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0285341/?ls). Taylor also found himself becoming successful in films as well. In 2005, he landed the role of Sharkboy in the family blockbuster flick, [The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl 3-D (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0424774/?ls), and the role of Eliot Murtaugh in [Cheaper by the Dozen 2 (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0452598/?ls). However, it would be one single role that would ultimately change Taylor's life forever. In 2008, Taylor auditioned for the iconic role of werewolf hunk Jacob Black in the record-smashing, blockbuster hit [Twilight (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1099212/?ls). With the sudden and unexpected success of the film, Taylor, along with fellow cast members [Robert Pattinson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1500155/?ls) and [Kristen Stewart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0829576/?ls), found himself being propelled into a world that would forever change his life and his career.  
  
Taylor has continued to portray Jacob Black in the following film adaptations of The Twilight Saga as well as branch out into other roles and films, such as the star-studded romantic comedy [Valentine's Day (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0817230/?ls) and the action-packed thriller [Abduction (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1600195/?ls). Taylor Lautner has quickly become one of the most famous, talented, and successful young Hollywood actors thanks to the blockbuster success of the [Twilight (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1099212/?ls) films. It has quickly been established by this young man's diverse and gifted talent that we will continue to be his audience for many years to come.

Her surname comes from her mother's Italian grandfather. Thanks to her mother, Kaya grew up fluent in Brazilian Portuguese, as well as English. At the age of fourteen, she auditioned for [Skins (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0840196/?ls), the debut series for new channel E4 that would become known for casting real teenagers like her, who had no professional acting experience, rather than experienced adult actors. She won the role of "Effy Stonem" and joined the show in January 2007. After an challenging debut in which she never spoke, Scodelario and Effy made quite an impression on viewers. At the forefront of many disasters, including stalkers, death, and sexual pressures, Effy became a fan favorite for her ability to resolve testing life situations while keeping her head above water. As the character and the role grew, Scodelario enjoyed depicting what she described as the realistic trials and challenges Effy faced with friendships, relationships, and adolescence. After two seasons of [Skins (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0840196/?ls), the series endured an overhaul at the end of 2007. Feeling that most of the characters had run their course, the writers wrote out every character except Effy. This put significantly more pressure on Scodelario because it meant that she would be the most recognizable face for season three. As she waited for the new season of [Skins (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0840196/?ls) to begin, she took advantage of her recent clout to seek out additional career opportunities. She joined the elite agency Models 1 and soon was featured as the cover model for SuperSuper Magazine. She made her feature film debut with a role in [Moon (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1182345/?ls), starring [Sam Rockwell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005377/?ls) as an astronaut suffering from surreal encounters while on the moon. With a blossoming film career and her successful TV series to fall back on, Kaya Scodelario is certainly someone to watch.

Haley Ramm has been making a name for herself over the past decade working alongside Hollywood veterans such as Jodie Foster, Sean Penn, Hope Davis, Jason Bateman and Peter Sarsgaard. Her innocent beauty coupled with her gritty roles in film and television have made her a standout among young Hollywood. Haley most recently starred in Hulu's thriller Light As A Feather and is well known from her starring role in the Freeform drama Chasing Life. She can next be seen starring opposite Keke Palmer in the Showtime film PIMP from Executive Producer Lee Daniels.  
  
At age three Haley Ramm, a Dallas native, started dancing in local studios. Her love of dancing on stage led to enrollment in acting classes and, at the recommendation of a teacher, her parents began looking for an agent. Almost immediately she signed an agency contract. After a few years of booking independent shorts and a slew of Hasbro commercials, Haley and her family ( with the help of her Dallas agent) discussed giving Los Angeles a shot.  
  
Upon making the move from Texas, she began booking roles and capturing audiences in co-star / guest-star roles and blockbuster films. After finding a manager in L.A., she booked small guest roles on CSI: Crime Scene Investigation (2000) and Yes, Dear (2000). Those television roles were followed by two national commercials. Then she booked what was to be her feature film debut in Rumor Has It... (2005). The Rob Reiner-directed film went through script rewrites and her role as "the young Jennifer Aniston" was cut to merely still shots. Soon after came Flightplan (2005). Just a few short months after completing "Flightplan" she booked the role of Kelly Beardsley, [Dennis Quaid](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000598/?ls)'s daughter, in the comedy [Yours, Mine & Ours (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0443295/?ls). It was another great opportunity to work with phenomenal actors. Dennis, [Rene Russo](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000623/?ls) and [Jerry O'Connell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005278/?ls) proved to be great role models with strong work ethics. Soon after came Into The Wild (2007), X-Men: The Last Stand (2006), Skateland (2010), Red State (2011) and Disconnect (2012). At the same time she was building her TV resume with a notable 6 episode arc on Without A Trace and guest stars on NCIS, iCarly, The Mentalist and Nikita. Since then Haley has steadily worked even while a series regular on Freeform's Chasing Life. During these years she shot Dakota's Summer [in which she stars as 'Dakota Rose' with Emily Rickards and Marin Hinkle], ImagiGary [directed by and starring The Middle's Charlie McDermott], and Victor [with Khleo Thomas], Blumhouse's Seven in Heaven, Banana Split [ Written by Hannah Marks and directed by Benjamin Kasulke].  
  
In 2015, she joined forces with AARDA (American Autoimmune Related Diseases Association) as a celebrity ambassador and together, with her mother who suffers from multiple autoimmune diseases, launched AARDA's "Linking Together For A Cure" walk in Los Angeles which is in its 4th year. Raising awareness and research money for these diseases is a passion for Ramm and she has successfully recruited support and spread awareness for AARDA.  
  
Haley currently resides in Los Angeles .

One of today's leading talents across both independent and mainstream film, Logan Lerman is an immensely talented actor who takes on challenging roles and brings dynamic characters to life on screen.  
  
Logan was born in Beverly Hills, to a Jewish family. His parents are Lisa (Goldman), who worked as his manager, and Larry Lerman, an orthotist and businessman. He has two siblings, Lindsey and Lucas, both older. His family operates the orthotics and prosthetics company Lerman & Son, which was founded by his great-grandfather, Jacob Lerman.  
  
When he was two and a half years old, Logan told his mother that he wanted to be an actor. At the age of four, Logan had an agent and was booked for two commercials. He made his big screen debut as William, the youngest son of [Mel Gibson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000154/?ls)'s character, in [Roland Emmerich](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000386/?ls)'s war drama [The Patriot (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0187393/?ls), and then appeared as the younger version of Gibson's character Nick Marshall in [Nancy Meyers](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0583600/?ls)'s romantic comedy [What Women Want (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0207201/?ls). After a small role in 2001's [Riding in Cars with Boys (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0200027/?ls) by [Penny Marshall](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001508/?ls), he starred in the [John Grisham](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001300/?ls) adaptation [A Painted House (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0362001/?ls), a made-for-television film that won him the first of his three Young Artist Awards.  
  
Logan played the younger version of [Ashton Kutcher](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005110/?ls)'s character, Evan, in [The Butterfly Effect (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0289879/?ls). After a guest-starring role in [10-8: Officers on Duty (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0365969/?ls), he starred in the WB Network's series [Jack & Bobby (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0410997/?ls), where he portrays Bobby (Robert) McCallister, a teenager who will grow up to be President of the United States. After the show's cancellation in 2005, Logan returned to film, starring in the family adventure [Hoot (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0453494/?ls). The next year, he played the son of Walter Sparrow ([Jim Carrey](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000120/?ls)) in the dark thriller [The Number 23 (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0481369/?ls), and co-starred with [Russell Crowe](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000128/?ls) and [Christian Bale](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000288/?ls) in [James Mangold](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0003506/?ls)'s critically-acclaimed Western remake [3:10 to Yuma (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0381849/?ls). His next two roles were a foul-mouthed private school student in the comedy [Meet Bill (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0790623/?ls) and actor [George Hamilton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001313/?ls) in the period drama [My One and Only (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1185431/?ls). Both were independent films that received limited releases. Also in 2009, Logan appeared with [Gerard Butler](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0124930/?ls) in the R-rated action thriller [Gamer (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1034032/?ls), as a foul-mouthed teenager who controls Butler's character in a real-life video game.  
  
In 2010, Logan starred as Percy in the fantasy adventure [Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0814255/?ls), based on the best-selling young adult book series of the same title. The film gave him notice among a wider audience. Subsequently, he starred as D'Artagnan in a remake of [The Three Musketeers (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1509767/?ls), which was Logan's grandfather's favorite childhood book. Lerman then headlined the coming-of-age indie drama [The Perks of Being a Wallflower (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1659337/?ls), alongside [Emma Watson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0914612/?ls), [Paul Rudd](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0748620/?ls) and [Ezra Miller](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3009232/?ls), based on the 1999 novel of the same name. Perks garnered numerous nominations and wins at the People's Choice Awards, The Independent Spirit Awards and the Teen Choice Awards, and Logan received a 2013 Teen Choice Award for Choice Movie Actor in a Drama. Around this time, he had a supporting role in the independent film [Stuck in Love. (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2205697/?ls), and returned to star in [Percy Jackson: Sea of Monsters (2013)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1854564/?ls).  
  
His first 2014 role was in [Darren Aronofsky](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004716/?ls)'s acclaimed Biblical epic film [Noah (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1959490/?ls), playing one of the title character's sons, Ham. The film, also starring [Russell Crowe](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000128/?ls), [Jennifer Connelly](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000124/?ls), [Anthony Hopkins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000164/?ls), [Douglas Booth](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3150488/?ls), and [Emma Watson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0914612/?ls), grossed over $100 million at the North American box office. In 2018, Logan voiced real-life soldier Robert Conroy in [Sgt. Stubby: An American Hero (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt5314190/?ls), about the famous World War I war dog. When Logan is not working, he likes to play soccer and baseball. He is an LA Lakers fan.

Taylor Daniel Lautner was born in Grand Rapids, Michigan, to Deborah, a software company worker, and Daniel Lautner, a pilot for Midwest Airlines. He and his younger sister Makena were raised in a well-mannered, Roman Catholic household in Hudsonville, Michigan. He is of English, German, Dutch, and Scottish descent. At the age of six, Taylor began studying martial arts at Fabiano's Karate School and he, along with his family, quickly noticed his unique and natural talent for the sport. He was soon invited to train with seven-time world karate champion Michael Chaturantabut (aka Mike Chat) and, at the age of eight, he was asked to represent his country in the 12-years-and-under division in the World Karate Association, where he became the Junior World Forms and Weapons champion, winning three gold medals. In 2003, Taylor continued to flourish in the martial arts circuit where he ranked number one in the world for NASKA's Black Belt Open Forms, Musical Weapons, Traditional Weapons, and Traditional Forms and, at the age of 12, he became the three-time Junior World Champion.  
  
However, in addition to his love for martial arts, Taylor quickly developed a love for acting at the age of seven years old when his martial arts instructor, who was involved in show business, encouraged him to audition for a small appearance in a Burger King commercial. Although he was unsuccessful, he enjoyed the experience so much that he told his parents that he wanted to pursue a career in acting. Soon, he and his family were traveling back and forth from their home in Michigan to California so Taylor could regularly audition for acting roles. When Taylor was 10, with the frequent traveling and air fares starting to become overwhelming, his family made the crucial decision to relocate to Los Angeles, where Taylor would have the advantage of being able to audition for films, television, and commercials full-time.  
  
Once Taylor moved with his family to Los Angeles, he found himself landing more and more small acting roles. He booked many occurring roles on various television shows such as [My Wife and Kids (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0273855/?ls), [Summerland (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0400037/?ls), and [The Bernie Mac Show (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0285341/?ls). Taylor also found himself becoming successful in films as well. In 2005, he landed the role of Sharkboy in the family blockbuster flick, [The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl 3-D (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0424774/?ls), and the role of Eliot Murtaugh in [Cheaper by the Dozen 2 (2005)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0452598/?ls). However, it would be one single role that would ultimately change Taylor's life forever. In 2008, Taylor auditioned for the iconic role of werewolf hunk Jacob Black in the record-smashing, blockbuster hit [Twilight (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1099212/?ls). With the sudden and unexpected success of the film, Taylor, along with fellow cast members [Robert Pattinson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1500155/?ls) and [Kristen Stewart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0829576/?ls), found himself being propelled into a world that would forever change his life and his career.  
  
Taylor has continued to portray Jacob Black in the following film adaptations of The Twilight Saga as well as branch out into other roles and films, such as the star-studded romantic comedy [Valentine's Day (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0817230/?ls) and the action-packed thriller [Abduction (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1600195/?ls). Taylor Lautner has quickly become one of the most famous, talented, and successful young Hollywood actors thanks to the blockbuster success of the [Twilight (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1099212/?ls) films. It has quickly been established by this young man's diverse and gifted talent that we will continue to be his audience for many years to come.
